newsitem.title: FRANCE: BELGIAN RENAULT WORKERS CLASH WITH FRENCH POLICE.
newsitem.headline: BELGIAN RENAULT WORKERS CLASH WITH FRENCH POLICE.

text.p: Four Renault workers were injured on Thursday when strikers from the car company's Belgian plant tried to force their way into the mayor's office in Lille, northern France, police said.

Police said 300 demonstrators protesting against Renault's plan to close the Vilvoorde plant had sought a hearing with Lille Mayor Pierre Mauroy, a former prime minister. After learning that Mauroy was in Paris, they tried to force their way into city hall and broke windows, prompting police to intervene.
Three workers were slightly injured and a fourth was taken to hospital, police said. Several workers were held for questioning.
Money-losing Renault announced on February 27 that it would close the plant, which employs 3,100 people, by the end of July to streamline its manufacturing operations and reduce costs.
Vilvoorde workers, who struck for six weeks after the announcement, resumed work on April 14 but were on strike again on Thursday.
Two courts in France and in Belgium ruled that Renault had breached the law in failing to consult staff ahead of the announcement but the rulings do not bear on the decision itself.
Renault Chairman Louis Schweitzer said he was flexible on the date and could postpone the closure by a few weeks or months but that the decision to shut down Vilvoorde was irrevocable.
